data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'wafa' meaning 'to honor, respect, or fulfill a promise'. In Islamic tradition, Awafita is a name for a girl who is deeply respectful, obedient, and loyal. The name Awafita carries the meaning “Honor or respect” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Awafita usually hope their child will grow to embody honor or respect and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.context: The Battle of Awafis (Awafita) took place in 632 AD, during the caliphate of Abu Bakr As-Siddiq, between the Muslim army led by Khalid ibn Al-Walid and the Byzantine forces led by the Roman Emperor Heraclius. The battle was fought near the city of Busra in modern-day Syria. The Muslims were victorious and this battle is considered one of the major military conquests during the early Islamic period.
